text:
maya: Quick design sync on the Autoscale/Capacity controls. I uploaded a new frame with two copy options and an updated burst pill rule. Need quick thumbs so eng can pick up. Figma: https://figma.redwood/infer/autoscale/variantX

sara: TL;DR for me: which guardrail label are we testing? 'Recommended cap' vs 'Safety cap'? And does the slider show numeric% or GPUs?

maya: Two variants: A = 'Recommended cap' (friendly), B = 'Safety cap' (stronger). We'll A/B test on the billing funnel. Default label shows absolute GPUs, but rule: if pool size > 16 show percent.

mike: Preference: 'Recommended cap'. Safer for self-serve. Also we should surface a tiny ephemeral note under slider: "How this affects availability" -> 2-line tooltip.

eden: Accessibility items: contrast of orange-50 on the guardrail fails WCAG AA at 12px. Suggest darken to #9A4A00 and add visible focus ring. Also need aria-live region for the slider value change.
sara: Good call. For the burst pill microcopy: what about two-line condensed state: line1: "+3 GPUs" line2 (muted): "(~+30%)" — shows both. Hover expands with explanation. Compact mobile view should only show percent.
mike: Love the compact idea. For extremely small pools (<4 GPUs) showing absolute can feel dramatic; maybe show percent there too? That could be confusing. Maybe rule: <=4 show absolute, 5-16 show absolute+muted%, >16 default to percent+muted absolute on hover.
maya: That mapping sounds reasonable. I'll update the spec: <=4 absolute, 5-16 absolute with percent muted, >16 percent primary.

eden: Keyboard UX: current pool selector traps focus because virtualization re-renders list. Implement roving tabindex and ensure Escape/Tab closes menu and returns focus to the toggle. Add a visible keyboard hint under the selector: "↑↓ preview • Enter select • Esc close".
sara: Copy nits: in the guardrail helper copy avoid 'throttle' — use 'may route to fallback capacity' (less scary). Also two test phrases for A/B: A uses 'Recommended cap' with helper 'Helps keep your latency within target.' B uses 'Safety cap' with helper 'Protects your SLO by limiting burst scale.' We'll test CTR on help link clicks and subsequent scale events.
mike: QA: can we add a tiny analytics event when users hover the percent vs absolute toggle? Want to measure which representation they prefer.

accessibility-bot: Logged issue ACC-4201: autoscale-guardrail-contrast + aria-live. Steps + screenshots attached. https://tracker.redwood/ACC-4201

maya: Plan: I will push updated frames with the percent/absolute rules and the two copy variants by EOD. Mike, can you add the analytics events? Eden, can you validate the contrast and aria-live once prototype is updated? Sara, I'll include you on the A/B test definition doc.
sara: Yes. I'll draft the hypothesis: "Friendly phrasing reduces configuration churn without increasing SLO breaches." Will post in doc.
mike: I'll add events: autoscale_guardrail_hover, burst_label_hover, pool_picker_keyboard_hint_shown. Ticket INF-3201 created.
eden: I'll test screenreader path and keyboard nav once prototype is live. Also recommend adding live region text: "Min set to X GPUs, Max set to Y GPUs. Guardrail: recommended at Z GPUs."
maya: Thanks all. Re-opening this thread when frames are uploaded. Closing for now. :white_check_mark:
